description: TrustAnchor stores owned Name and SubjectPublicKeyInfoOwned rather than borrowing from a certificate. This is correct because anchors live independently of any certificate — a platform trust store stores (name, SPKI) pairs, not full certificate DER. Borrowing from Certificate would force callers to keep Certificate alive for the trust anchor lifetime. ValidatedPath being #[non_exhaustive] is also correct: it currently has anchor_index and depth, and future additions (e.g. validated_policies, name_constraints_result) will be common. Making it non_exhaustive now avoids a breaking change later. A contributor might suggest making ValidatedPath::new() available for testing — that would defeat the purpose of non_exhaustive. The current design is correct.
title: TrustAnchor stores owned data; ValidatedPath is non_exhaustive — both correct
